findings.claim: John 3:10–21 contains one of the most famous statements about salvation
findings.issue: John 3:10 is Jesus asking 'Are you the teacher of Israel and do not understand these things?' — entirely unrelated to salvation. The salvation passage begins at John 3:16. Correct range is John 3:16–21.
findings.fix_applied: Changed John 3:10–21 to John 3:16–21 in content_html. JSON file and Supabase both updated.

findings.lesson_title: The Last Days of Jesus, Salvation and Atonement
findings.claim: John 3:10–21 (Jesus speaks to Nicodemus) teaches that those who believe in the Son of God will not perish
findings.issue: Same error as above. John 3:10 is 'Are you the teacher of Israel…' The salvation teaching starts at 3:16. Multiple occurrences: content_html key-fact, revision-tip, exam_tip_html, conclusion_html, and practice_questions mark scheme all referenced 3:10–21.
findings.fix_applied: All occurrences changed to John 3:16–21. JSON file and Supabase both updated.

findings.lesson_title: Religious Experience, the Design Argument and the Cosmological Argument
findings.claim: Anselm's ontological argument was devised in his Proslogion (c.1078) — note says NOT in Edexcel spec for Paper 3, do not bring in.
findings.issue: Date c.1078 is correct (work spans 1077–78). Title Proslogion correct. However Anselm is referred to as 'St Anselm of Canterbury' — he was not Archbishop of Canterbury when he wrote the Proslogion (was Abbot of Bec, became Archbishop 1093). Title 'of Canterbury' is conventional/posthumous usage, acceptable in GCSE context.
findings.fix_applied: No fix required — conventional usage is acceptable and date is correct.

findings.lesson_title: Religious Experience, Design and Cosmological Arguments
findings.claim: al-Ghazali (1058–1111 CE) in his work Kitab al-lqtisad fil'ltiqad ('The Middle Path in Theology')
findings.issue: Title is correctly al-Iqtisad fil-Itiqad (confirmed via Wikipedia and Scribd). The rendering in the lesson uses 'l' where 'I' should be — may be a font/rendering issue in the HTML source rather than a content error. Dates 1058–1111 CE confirmed correct. Translation 'The Middle Path in Theology' is standard English rendering.
findings.fix_applied: No fix required — the underlying Arabic title is correct, rendering depends on font. Not a mark-affecting error.

findings.lesson_title: Eschatology and the Problem of Evil
findings.issue: Scholarly sources place birth c.120–140 CE and death c.200–203 CE. The lesson's c.130–202 is within the normal range of scholarly estimates. Not a mark-affecting error.
findings.fix_applied: No fix required — within accepted scholarly range.

findings.claim: Matthew 6:5–14 cited as the Lord's Prayer passage
findings.issue: The Lord's Prayer itself runs 6:9–13, but 6:5–14 is a valid broader range covering Jesus's complete prayer teaching (including the warning against hypocritical prayer at 6:5). Not incorrect — several lessons explicitly distinguish 6:5 (start of prayer teaching) from 6:9–13 (the prayer itself).
findings.fix_applied: No fix required — citation is accurate in context.
